title: The Wisdom of God
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The wisdom of God means that God perfectly knows, orders, and accomplishes what is best according to His holy purpose. His wisdom is deeper than human understanding and always joined to His goodness, power, and truth.
summary: The wisdom of God means that God perfectly knows, orders, and accomplishes what is best according to His holy purpose. His wisdom is deeper than human understanding and always joined to His goodness, power, and truth.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the wisdom of God revealed for salvation. In Him are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge, and through Him God’s saving plan is displayed.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
God’s wisdom is perfect. He never misjudges, miscalculates, or lacks understanding. He orders creation, history, salvation, judgment, and providence according to His own holy purpose.

The world often sees God’s wisdom as foolishness, especially in the cross of Christ. Yet what appears weak or foolish to sinful people is the power and wisdom of God.

God’s wisdom is not abstract. It is revealed in creation, providence, Scripture, and supremely in Jesus Christ. In Christ, God saves sinners in a way no human wisdom could invent.

Believers are invited to ask God for wisdom. The wise God does not shame His children for needing help; He gives wisdom generously to those who seek Him in faith.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People often trust their own understanding until life exposes its limits. Suffering, temptation, decisions, conflict, and delay reveal how much wisdom we lack.

This doctrine teaches humble dependence. God’s wisdom is not always immediately understandable, but it is always trustworthy. The cross proves that God’s ways are higher and better than ours.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Seek wisdom from God instead of leaning on your own understanding. Bring decisions, confusion, suffering, and counsel under Scripture and prayer. Trust Christ as the wisdom of God, and walk in humility when God’s ways are deeper than your explanations.
